headline: Permitting and Inspection Requirements for Driveways in Los Angeles County
articleBody: Driveway permitting in Los Angeles County depends on whether the work is fully on private property or involves the public right-of-way, such as the apron or curb cut. The City of Los Angeles Bureau of Engineering states that a permit is required for construction, reconstruction, or alteration of driveways that connect to city streets, including removal and replacement of driveway aprons and curb modifications. Similar requirements appear in many incorporated cities across the county, where public works or engineering departments regulate driveway approaches to maintain sidewalk integrity, drainage, and traffic safety. For work entirely within private property, some jurisdictions allow replacement in kind without a building permit if grades and drainage are not changed, while others treat substantial concrete or grading work as requiring permits. The Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety explains that grading above certain thresholds, retaining walls, or changes that alter drainage patterns may trigger plan review under local building codes and the California Residential Code. Los Angeles County Public Works publishes driveway and encroachment permit requirements for unincorporated areas, covering access to county-maintained roads. These standards address driveway width, slope, sight distance, and drainage to prevent water from discharging onto the roadway. Inspections typically occur after base preparation and again after placement to verify conformance with approved plans and standard drawings. Consumer advice from the California Contractors State License Board emphasizes that property owners are usually responsible for ensuring the correct permits are obtained, even when contractors handle the paperwork. It recommends confirming directly with the local building or public works department before work begins and obtaining final inspection sign-off to document compliance for future property disclosures or refinancing.
